_comment: Folders the contract cannot generate, appended to the generated collection.
Two kinds live here and they are kept apart deliberately.
The conformance folders assert controls by sending requests a well-behaved
client would never send. A contract describes what is allowed; these check
what happens when something else arrives, which is where the interesting
failures are. Every one of them runs against an endpoint that exists today.
pendingPaths lists surface that is specified and not built yet, so a 404 on
one of those paths is reported as 'not implemented yet' rather than as a
red row hiding the rows that matter. The determination folder asserts the
controls on the endpoints that exist, and runs only when asked to.
Edit this file, then run `npm run postman` in contracts/. Editing the

folders.name: 05 · Contract conformance — with a session
folders.description:
Requests a well-behaved client would never send, to endpoints that need a session. Each asserts a control, and each runs against an endpoint that exists today — so a green row here is evidence rather than an aspiration.

They sit before `08 · Sign out` because they need the session it ends; after it they could only return 401, which is evidence of nothing but the run order.

requests.name: Unknown field is rejected, not ignored
requests.description:
ADR-0011 §2.1 P5 at the transport boundary.

Silently dropping an undeclared field would let two different requests digest identically, which is exactly the property an idempotency record depends on (ADR-0013 §2.4). It is also the common shape of a real integration bug: a client sends `displayname` where the contract says `displayName`, and a server that ignores it creates a user with no display name and reports success.
test: pm.test('a field the contract does not declare is rejected', function () {

requests.name: Explicit null is rejected
requests.description:
ADR-0011 §2.1 P3.

"Explicitly cleared" and "not supplied" are different facts with different consequences, and a canonical form that collapses them erases the difference from the evidence too. So `null` is an error rather than something to normalise.
test: pm.test('an explicit null is refused rather than normalised', function () {

requests.name: A role outside the closed set is refused
requests.description:
`Role` is a closed enum in the contract. Adding one is a reviewed change with an authorization-matrix entry, not a string a caller may invent — and a server that stored an unrecognised role would be a server whose authorization decisions nobody can audit.

Needs `userId`, which `04 · Administration` captures.
test: pm.test('an invented role is refused', function () {

folders.name: 90 · Contract conformance — without a session
folders.description: The same kind of request, for the controls that are about having no session at all — an unauthenticated caller, a sign-in that fails, a path nothing routes. They run after `08 · Sign out` so the cookie jar holds no session to send.

requests.name: An unrouted path is still a Problem
requests.description:
ADR-0016 §2.5: every error a client sees has one shape, including the one `net/http.ServeMux` would otherwise answer with plain text.

A client that has to parse two error formats parses one of them badly.
test: pm.test('a 404 is a Problem Details document, not plain text', function () {

requests.name: An administrative endpoint refuses an unauthenticated caller
requests.description:
The session cookie is deliberately cleared for this request only.

It asserts the distinction ADR-0016 §2.5 draws between 401 and 403: this is "we do not know who you are", and the client action is to sign in. A 403 here would tell a caller to ask for a role, which would not help.
test: pm.test('no session is UNAUTHENTICATED, not FORBIDDEN', function () {

requests.name: Sign-in does not distinguish a wrong password from an unknown user
requests.description:
Both answers are `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`.

Distinguishing them is an account-enumeration oracle, and a caller can do nothing with the difference. Run this and the next request together: the reason code must be identical in both.
test: pm.test('an unknown subject is INVALID_CREDENTIALS', function () {

requests.name: …and neither does a wrong password for a real user
requests.description: The pair with the request above. The assertion is not that this is a 401 — it is that the reason code is the *same* one, so nothing in the response tells a caller whether the address exists.
test: pm.test('a wrong password is INVALID_CREDENTIALS', function () {
pm.test('it is indistinguishable from an unknown subject', function () {

folders.name: 07 · Determination conformance — needs content and an OPERATOR
folders.description:
The ADR-0013 and ADR-0011 controls on `POST /v1/transactions:commit`, each asserted against the running endpoint.

Requests 1 to 4 share one idempotency key, minted once per run into `reusedKey`, so a second run against the same cell exercises the same four outcomes rather than replaying the first run's.

Skipped unless `runDetermination` is `"true"`, for the reason `06` gives.

requests.name: Idempotency · 1 · first commit with a fixed key
requests.description: ADR-0013 §2.4. The first of four: this one establishes the record, and requests 2 to 4 are the interesting ones.

requests.name: Idempotency · 2 · same key, same body
requests.description: Must return the *original* response, byte for byte, and record nothing. A retry that produced a second decision would be a second fiscal record for one transaction, which is the Critical risk in Build Plan §8.
test: pm.test('the retry is the original response, verbatim', function () {

requests.name: Idempotency · 3 · same key, DIFFERENT body
requests.description:
Must be a 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSE` and must not execute (ADR-0013 §2.4).

Replaying the original response would be worse than either alternative: the caller would believe the amount it sent was the amount recorded.
test: pm.test('a reused key is refused, not replayed', function () {

requests.name: Idempotency · 4 · same key, same value at a different scale
requests.description:
`"45.0"` is not `"45.00"`. Scale is semantic (ADR-0011 §2.2), so the canonical request digest differs and this is a different request under a used key.

A server that compared parsed numbers would replay request 1 here, and hand back a decision made at a precision the caller did not send.
test: pm.test('scale is part of the request', function () {

requests.name: Idempotency · 5 · no key at all
requests.description: `Idempotency-Key` is mandatory on `:commit`, `:adjust`, `:refund` and `POST /v1/batches` (ADR-0013 §2.1). Rejected before any work begins.
test: pm.test('a keyless commit is refused', function () {

requests.name: Canonical form · a fiscal amount sent as a JSON number
requests.description:
**The request in this collection that matters most.**

`"amount": 45.0` must be rejected, never coerced. A 2xx here is a Critical finding rather than a test failure: RFC 8785 serializes JSON numbers through IEEE 754 doubles (ADR-0011 §1.1), so an amount that is ever a JSON number has lost precision before canonicalization sees it — and the loss is invisible, because 45.0 survives and 0.1 does not.

The body is raw text rather than a structured one, because the whole point is to send a token a correct client cannot produce.
test: pm.test('a JSON number is never an amount', function () {

requests.name: Canonical form · explicit null in a fiscal position
requests.description: ADR-0011 §2.1 P3 on the path where it costs the most. "The amount was explicitly cleared" and "the integration did not send an amount" are different events with different fiscal consequences.
test: pm.test('null is refused rather than normalised', function () {

requests.name: Canonical form · a miscased field inside the input
requests.description: ADR-0011 P5 below the top level. `Currency` beside `currency` is refused, not matched case-insensitively: encoding/json would otherwise let the later key win, and the decision would be recorded in whichever currency happened to come last.
test: pm.test('an undeclared nested field is refused', function () {
